text: Planning Commission Chair, City of Cupertino
Repeatedly, residents have asked Cupertino to be fiscally responsible, to grow thoughtfully, and to prioritize their safety.
I am running to deliver on these shared goals that unite us. Our residents and businesses can't afford to watch as progress solving real problems is stalled by political agendas.

In the past few years, I approved new housing in the heart of our city, while supporting balanced zoning to protect businesses and neighborhoods. I stood firm on upholding safety and emergency response times. And I opposed cost-of-living increases, like new freeway express lane tolls.
When I work with the public on the Cupertino Planning Commission, I seek to listen to people, not punish them because they have the audacity to ask challenging questions.

I am a lifelong Cupertino resident, graduating from Monta Vista High School before earning my degree from UPenn's Wharton School. My husband and I returned to raise our two young kids in a truly collaborative and world-class environment.

Unlike the cacophony of competing interests seeking to divide us, I will take the time to engage our community and deliver real results. I would be honored to earn your vote. Learn more at VoteTracyK.com

text: City Commissioner; Teacher; Mentor; Technology Executive (AI)

I have dedicated my life to investing in people because I believe the strongest communities are built by connecting people. For 25+ years, I have served our community as a teacher, mentor, and volunteer.

During the past 10 years, I proudly served on Cupertino's Parks and Recreation Commission, Library Commission, and Cupertino Library Foundation. I helped advance the Parks and Recreation System Master Plan, supported library expansion, created the City's all-inclusive playground, expanded the dog off-leash area, strengthened recreation programs, and recommended funding for local nonprofits.

Every weekend for 25 years, I have taught preschool children, mentored students, parents, and professionals, and helped seniors improve digital literacy and stay safe from online scams. I also serve on the Board of Hope Services, supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and mental health needs.
Professionally, I have led global technology organizations and serve as an executive advisor on AI and digital transformation.
My family has proudly called Cupertino home for many years, and our children attended Cupertino schools.

If elected, I will put Residents First, bring people together, preserve quality of life, and strengthen opportunities for students, seniors, families, local businesses and City staff. www.Gopal4Cupertino.org

text: Nonprofit Director
Imagine Cupertino buzzing with life—new restaurants, exciting businesses, fresh entertainment and recreation opportunities. It's time for leadership that delivers real results for residents.

My husband and I moved to Cupertino twenty years ago to raise our family. With an MBA from Carnegie Mellon University, I built a 20-year career as a marketing leader for Fortune 500 companies before turning that drive toward serving residents in our community.

I served 12 years as a Safe Routes to School and PTA parent. As Chair of Walk Bike Cupertino, I delivered real results: the Regnart Creek Trail, safer school streets, intersections, and connected sidewalks. Since 2023, I have served as Cupertino Planning Commissioner, where I scaled down developments to better fit housing into neighborhoods, cut permitting red tape for small home upgrades, streamlined ADU permitting, and won approval for more trees citywide, especially east Cupertino.

My priorities are set by residents: create a real downtown at Vallco, cut bureaucratic red tape, attract mid-sized businesses for diversified revenue and more resident choices, and build safer neighborhoods.

I am endorsed by Senator Josh Becker, Assemblymembers Patrick Ahrens and Alex Lee, Supervisor Margaret Abe-Koga, Assessor Neysa Fligor, Councilmember (former Mayor) Sheila Mohan, and eight other former Mayors. I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: Technology Executive, Cupertino Planning Commissioner

I have worked in Cupertino since 1999 and have called it home since 2015. As 2025 Chair of the Cupertino Planning Commission and a member of the CUSD Bond Oversight Committee overseeing $350 million in school bonds, I have dedicated myself to serving our community.

As a technology executive with 30 years of leadership experience, I bring sound judgment, fiscal responsibility, and accountability to public service. On the Planning Commission, I have reviewed major housing proposals, supporting well-planned housing while protecting established neighborhoods.
As a school parent and community volunteer, I have worked with residents, seniors, and schools to improve quality of life and ensure local government listens to our community.

If elected to the Cupertino City Council, I will work to maximize quality of life, strengthen public safety, support excellent schools, invest wisely in infrastructure, protect our neighborhoods, and spend taxpayer dollars responsibly.

text: Civil Engineer
I am a California professional engineer with degrees from UC Davis and San Jose State University.
I bring more than 50 years of engineering design experience serving communities throughout the Bay Area.
I am running for Cupertino City Council because I believe our city government has lost sight of common-sense solutions to the issues facing Cupertino.
Government authority is held in trust for the people and must remain accountable to the residents it serves.
After attending planning and council hearings, I have observed residents dismissed when expressing concerns about development in their neighborhoods.
I believe state housing mandates are steadily reducing local control and weakening zoning protections that residents have relied upon for decades.
I oppose policies that place growth ahead of neighborhood protections, public safety, and property rights. I will fight for common sense, local control, and respect for Cupertino residents.
Email: info@fantozziforcupertino.com
Website: fantozziforcupertino.com

text: Member of the City Council/Attorney

I'm a third-generation Cupertino resident. My family arrived here in the Valley of Heart's Delight in 1952. I grew up here, attended our schools, graduated from UCLA, and returned to Silicon Valley. That thriving Cupertino gave residents so much. I'm running for reelection to ensure future generations get that same chance.

As your councilmember, I've used my expertise as an attorney to get real results for residents. I expanded housing for teachers, seniors, and young families─while keeping our small-town feel─by winning state approval for Cupertino's housing plan. I helped negotiate a state tax deal that saved our city millions securing a balanced budget. I fought for better infrastructure, greater public safety, and a government that follows the law and listens to you.

We need strong partnerships to accomplish big things for Cupertino─and I've built them as Vice President of the Cities Association of Santa Clara County and as our representative to Silicon Valley Clean Energy, and the Santa Clara County Library District.

Our residents deserve a future where every generation, at every income level, can afford to stay and thrive in Cupertino. That's why Assemblymembers Patrick Ahrens and Alex Lee, Senator Josh Becker, Supervisor Margaret Abe-Koga, Councilmember Sheila Mohan, and nine former Cupertino mayors support me.
Vote for me─we'll build a thriving Cupertino together. jr4cupertino.com

text: Educator/Engineer/Executive

Cupertino has been my home for 17 years and the longest I have lived anywhere in one place. My wife and I are proud to raise our two sons here. As a refugee, I am deeply grateful to call Cupertino home.

A licensed Professional Engineer with an MBA from Columbia University, my 30-year career spans executive leadership in engineering, finance, and public affairs. My service to residents and the community at large includes serving as Cupertino Chamber of Commerce President and Pack 492 Cubmaster, and teaching engineering as an adjunct professor at San José State University for nearly two decades.

Here's why I'm running: Cupertino faces a critical financial and development crossroads. We need transparent, accountable leadership that puts residents first. I know firsthand how to secure infrastructure, manage multimillion-dollar budgets, and unite diverse leaders to solve shared challenges. I will champion policies that put residents first by creating housing for every stage of life, upgrading our water system, roads and facilities, and strengthening our local economy.

I am endorsed by Congressman Sam Liccardo, Assemblymembers Patrick Ahrens and Alex Lee, Supervisor Margaret Abe-Koga, Assessor Neysa Fligor, Councilmember and former Mayor Sheila Mohan, and ten other former Cupertino Mayors.
I respectfully ask for your vote.
